fullAddress: Minnewaska State Park Preserve, NY
title: SRBP Lecture Series: Shale Under Siege--Gasland Screening & Discussion
desc: With Cara Lee, Shawangunk Ridge Program Director, The Nature Conservancy, and Nadia Steinzor, Marcellus Regional Organizer, EARTHWORKS Oil & Gas Accountability Project. Across the globe and close to home, the race for new sources of energy is on, with natural gas currently in the lead. The Marcellus Shale region is slated by industry for extensive gas development using the controversial technique of horizontal hydraulic fracturing or "fracking." The documentary Gasland has been critical to raising awareness and sparking discussion on the issue. After the screening, there will be a discussion about what the gas rush could mean for communities, landowners, and landscapes in this region and how you can get involved. This lecture will take place at the Ellenville Public Library.

fullAddress: Schoharie Crossing State Historic Site, NY
title: Springtime Walks and Workshops: Dream Catchers: A Native American Tradition
desc: Fee $35 per person. Registration required! CallVisitor Center to register. Historically, the Native Americans of the Great Plains hung the dream catchers in the tipi or lodge, and also on a baby's cradle board. Legend has it that the good dreams pass through the center hole to the sleeping person. The bad dreams are trapped in the web where they perish in the light of dawn. Mohawk Zelda Hotaling will show you how to recycle the fibers of the earth to create your own custom piece. Like the tipi, the dream catcher has become a universal symbol of the Pan-American Movement. Visit www.zeldahotaling.com for more info

title: First Spring Weekend Walk
desc: Join Park Preserve educator Jillian Koehnken for an interpretive two-and-a-half mile walk along the Awosting Falls Carriage Road. Our destination is the beautiful Awosting Falls, a 65-foot tall waterfall that creates incredible ice formations every winter and turns into a powerful, roaring cascade with the winter snow melt. fullAddress: Fort Montgomery State Historic Site, NY
title: Winter/Spring Walk Series: Appalachian Trail History Hike
desc: The Appalachian Trail is well known but its history is not. Did you know that the original leg of the trail was built at Trailside Museums and Zoo (the Bear Mountain Zoo) in 1923? Or that the trail was originally designed to connect a series of farms and wilderness work/study camps for city-dwellers? On this ramble discover little known facets of the trail while hiking it. We will hike from Fort Montgomery State Historic Site to the newly rerouted section of the trail on Bear Mountain, talking mainly history, but in original tradition of the trail, stopping along the way to take in items of natural interest including indigenous plants, animals, trees, and geology. This is an intermediate/difficult hike, so bring your boots, water and a snack! All programming free--donations appreciated!

Wade in the Schoharie Creek, grab a net and then look under a microscope to see what is living in the water.   Noon --Join us for a walking tour along the towpath trail. See the remains of the Original Erie Canal and the Enlarged Erie Canal including the East Guard Lock, Lock #20, the Empire Lock, Lock 30 and the Schoharie Aqueduct.   Fee $3 for adults, $2 seniors, and $1 for children under 16.  1:00 pm to 5:00 pm, if you arrive at the Visitor Center by bike or on foot, you will receive a free gift and 10% off in the gift shop.  For the entire month of June, if you stop in at the Visitor Center prior to launching your boat, canoe or kayak, you will receive a free gift.

Round trip will be just over a mile.

title: Winter/Spring Walk Series: Eco-lutionary--Unintentionally "Green" in the 1700's
desc: In this slide presentation and hands-on, show and tell, Fort Montgomery State Historic Site interpreter Peter Cutul will present some of the numerous and innovative ways our colonial ancestors reduced, re-used and recycled. With an eye out always out for the useful, the program will conclude with practical tidbits we can take away, as well as those prectices perhaps better left in the past! title: SRBP Lecture Series:  What’s Bugging Our Forests
desc:
What's Bugging Our Forests. With Chris Zimmerman, Conservation Ecologist, The Nature Conservancy. New York forests are under siege by non-native pest and pathogens. For many of the tree species in our preserves, working forests and backyards, there is a destructive invasive pest or pathogen. This past summer, Emerald Ash Borer (EAB) was found in Ulster and Greene Counties. EAB is responsible for the death or decline of tens of millions of ash trees in 14 states. Asian longhorn beetle is in New York City, New Jersey and Massachusetts, and kills maples, birch and willow. Learn how to identify these insects and what you can do to stop their spread. This lecture will take place at the Ellenville Public Library & Museum.

Composed of non-profit and public agencies including Minnewaska, the Shawangunk Ridge Biodiversity Partnership is dedicated to protecting the sensitive wildlife habitat and other natural resources of the Shawangunk Mountains. This series will present five different lectures about the conservation work underway across the region to protect and manage wildlife and natural systems. The series combines four lectures in New Paltz and two in Ellenville.  Lectures will be held on Thursdays through March and are open to the public and free of charge.

title: Springtime Walks and Workshops: Dream Catchers: A Native American Tradition
desc: Fee $35 per person. Registration required! Call Visitor Center to register. Historically, the Native Americans of the Great Plains hung the dream catchers in the tipi or lodge, and also on a baby's cradle board. Legend has it that the good dreams pass through the center hole to the sleeping person. The bad dreams are trapped in the web where they perish in the light of dawn. Mohawk Zelda Hotaling will show you how to recycle the fibers of the earth to create your own custom piece. Like the tipi, the dream catcher has become a universal symbol of the Pan-American Movement. Visit www.zeldahotaling.com for more info

title: Winter/Spring Walk Series: Appalachian Trail History Hike
desc: The Appalachian Trail is well known but its history is not.  Did you know that the original leg of the trail was built at Trailside Museums and Zoo (the Bear Mountain Zoo) in 1923? Or that the trail was originally designed to connect a series of farms and wilderness work/study camps for city-dwellers?  On this ramble discover little known facets of the trail while hiking it.  We will hike from Fort Montgomery State Historic Site to the newly rerouted section of the trail on Bear Mountain, talking mainly history, but in original tradition of the trail, stopping along the way to take in items of natural interest including indigenous plants, animals, trees, and geology.  This is an intermediate/difficult hike, so bring your boots, water and a snack!  All programming free--donations appreciated!

fullAddress: Lorenzo State Historic Site, NY
title: Horses in History and at Lorenzo
desc: When horses and carriages were the norm of transportation, the village of Cazenovia was characterized by numerous carriage stables, hitching posts and blacksmith shops. Today, Lorenzo State Historic Site is home to an extensive collection of horse-drawn vehicles and a renowned annual pleasure driving competition. In celebration of the 35th Annual Lorenzo Driving Competition, and in association with the Cazenovia Public Library's equine-centered series of programs this spring, a special family program will be held on Saturday, April 9 at the Lorenzo visitor center. Program participants will learn how to identify breeds of horse, meet a miniature horse—or two (courtesy Cazenovia College), receive a guided tour of the Lorenzo carriage and sleigh collection and find out how these vehicles were used throughout the year. Special horse-related handouts and giveaways will be available to all participants, 12 and under, and refreshments will be served. Admission is free and open to the public, but pre-registration by April 5 is required as space is limited. Sponsored by the Lorenzo Driving Competition, Inc.

fullAddress: Minnewaska State Park Preserve, NY
title: Earth Day Volunteer Trails Day Event
desc: In honor of Earth Day, Minnewaska State Park Preserve is looking for volunteers to help improve our trails. Participants will work with Park Preserve staff as well as with trained and experienced volunteers of the New York-New Jersey Trail Conference. Volunteers will use hand tools to clip back an overgrown footpath and clear it of any debris left behind by storms this past winter. Families and individuals are invited to join us for this fun day outside during which they can gain valuable experience, make new friends and contribute to the improvement of trail conditions for all users. This event is also a great way for students in public school to accrue necessary community service hours for completion of their requirements. This program is recommended for adults and teenagers, who must be accompanied by an adult over the age of 18 years. Participants are encouraged to bring their own work gloves and tools including loppers, bow saws and clipping shears. The parking fee will be waived for participants volunteering for this program. Please wear appropriate clothing, sturdy hiking shoes, and bring plenty of snacks, water and lunch. Pre-registration is required.

fullAddress: Olana State Historic Site, NY
title: Framing the Viewshed: The Transformative Power of Art and Landscape in the Hudson Valley
desc: Viewsheds are an intrinsic part of every nationally significant region. America's first art and conservation movement had deep roots in the Hudson Valley, and thissymposium, hosted by The Olana Partnership, will offer a fresh look aticonic Hudson Valley scenes through the lens of art history, environmental conservation, and landscape architecture. Featuring lectures by Linda S. Ferber, Vice-President & Senior Art Historian, New-York Historical Society, Harvey K. Flad, Emeritus Professor of Geography, Vassar College, Laurie Olin, OLIN / Partner, RLA, FASLA, and moderated by David Schuyler, Arthur and Katherine Shadek Professor of the Humanities and Professor of American Studies, Franklin & Marshall College.Please join us as we span three centuries of thought and explore historic and contemporary perspectives on the famed "borrowed views" of the Hudson Valley. $40 Members/$50 Non-members/$10 Students. Registration begins at 12:30PM.

fullAddress: Minnewaska State Park Preserve, NY
title: Lurking in the Trees- Film and Walk
desc: It started when a sinister-looking bug fell on someone's lap in a back yard on a summer afternoon. That chance discovery led to a terrible realization: insect-invaders...were killing trees in New England, and the only way to stop the pests was to cut down and grind up over 25,000 trees" (TNC, 2009). Come to the Minnewaska Nature Center for a screening of the brief film, Lurking in the Trees, a documentary by The Nature Conservancy on one of the many invasive species threatening our forests. Following the film will be a brief walk on the trails near Lake Minnewaska, where we will discuss identifying these insects, the signs they leave behind, and what could happen if they come to your area. This program is recommended for adults and children nine years old and up, accompanied by a parent or guardian over the age of 18 years old.

fullAddress: Olana State Historic Site, NY
title: Exhibition: Rally 'Round the Flag: Frederic Edwin Church and the Civil War
desc: Thursdays-Sundays, 11:00AM - 4:00PM. Two weeks before the scheduled debut of Hudson River School landscape painter Frederic Church's masterwork The Icebergs, Fort Sumter was bombarded marking the start of the American Civil War. Instead of cancelling the unveiling of the painting at Goupil's Gallery, Church re-titled his masterpiece: "The North" Church's Picture of Icebergs showing his support for the northern cause. Church also pledged exhibition fees to assist the Union's Patriotic Fund for the families of Union soldiers. Less than a month later, in further support, and in response to the patriotic fever that swept the North, in May 1861 Church painted Our Banner in the Sky – a sunrise resembling a Union Flag. The image became a popular chromolithograph issued by Goupil & Co. 2011 will mark the Sesquicentennial of the fall of Fort Sumter and the start of the Civil War. Olana's exhibition will examine Church's reaction to the conflict as an artist and how events involving his friends and colleagues affected him personally. The exhibition will include: 4 oil sketches by Church; 2 pencil sketches by Church; 2 chromolithographs after Church; and works by Isaac Hayes and John Jameson.

On Saturday, Liaison Plaisant, an ensemble featuring music for clavichord, cello, whistles and percussion, will present a series of melodies known throughout the Hudson and Mohawk Valleys. On Sunday, join us for an afternoon of ballads, drinking songs, dance music and more performed by Balladeer Linda Russell and Companie. Concerts both days will be held 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Bring your own chairs or picnic blanket.   The mansion will also be available free of charge for Open House (self-guided) tours, 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Suggested donation: $3.00.   For more information about New York Heritage Weekend, please visit www.heritageweekend.org   (Please note: In the event of inclement weather, concerts will be moved indoors with limited seating while Open House will be limited to first floor of mansion only.)
